title: The context generation TermAl reports to Engram restarts from termal-1 after a host restart
outcome: The token TermAl passes on a session's orientation read (`work next --peek --context-generation termal-<n>`) is never reused by that session across host restarts, so Engram can tell a new context from one it has already acknowledged. Either the token carries a host-incarnation part beside the counter, or the counter is preserved in the persisted session; the choice is recorded on the item with its reason.
acceptance: A session restored after a host restart never sends a context-generation token it sent before the restart: a test restores a persisted session whose generation had advanced and reads the token of its next orientation read.

Engram's coordinator has confirmed in a note or by mailbox, cited by message number, that the token's new form is accepted by `work next --peek --context-generation` and by the `memories --context-generation` argument Engram is adding.

Every token the host builds is a plain token as Engram will enforce it: 1 to 256 characters, only ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore and dash, not starting with a dash; a test checks the exact token, including the host-incarnation part, against that rule.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and diff hash cited in a note.

Within one host run the token still changes exactly when it does today (a compaction, a replacement, the other existing bumps) and not otherwise; the existing context-nudge tests pass, with any changed expectation listed in a note with its reason.
